header.running_head: Condemning Rulers who Live Lives Above the Standards of the Common People and who Veil Themselves from people in Need

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Bakrah (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA)
blocks.text: Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Bakrah (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) states that the news that reached Hadhrat Umar (RA) stated that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) kept aloof from the people and locked them out of his house. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then dispatched Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir (RA) with instructions to go to Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) and if he found the door locked, he was to burn it down. [^1]
The Incident Between Hadhrat Umar (RA) and a group of Sahabah (RA) in Shaam

Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once sought permission from Hadhrat Umar (RA) to go to Shaam. Hadhrat Umar (RA) told him that he would be allowed to go there only on condition that he became a governor of one of the areas. When Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) refused to be a governor, Hadhrat Umar (RA) refused to grant the permission. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) then said, "I shall go there to teach people the Sunnah of their Nabi ﷺ and lead them in salaah." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then granted him permission.
Hadhrat Umar (RA) later visited Shaam and when he drew close to where the Sahabah (RA) were staying, he stopped until evening fell. When the night cast its veil over him, he called to his slave saying, "O Yarfa! Let us go to Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan (RA). You will see that he has story-tellers with him, lanterns will be burning and rugs of silk[^2] and velvet will be spread out, which have been taken from the booty belonging to the Muslims. You will greet him and he will reply, after which you will ask permission to enter and he will not grant permission until he enquires who you are."
The two men proceeded until they reached the door of Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) greeted by saying, "As Salaamu Alaykum!" to which Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) replied, "Wa Alaykumus Salaam." When Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked whether he could enter, Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) first asked, "Who are you?" To this Yarfa replied, "This is the one who is about to spoil your fun. This is the Ameerul Mu'mineen." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then opened the door and found story-tellers there, lanterns burning and rugs of silk and velvet. Hadhrat Umar (RA) urgently instructed Yarfa to shut the door and struck Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) with his whip right between the ears. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then folded up all the goods and placed it at the centre of the room. He then issued the command that no one should move until he returned.
Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Yarfa then left Hadhrat Yazeed (RA). Hadhrat Umar

entire narration is reported in Isaaba (Vol.3 Pg.384) except that the narrator's name appears as Abaaya bin Rifaa'ah instead of Attaab bin Rifaa'ah. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.167) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.168) has commented on the chain of narrators.

These rugs may not have been pure silk, but a mixture of silk and more of another fabric. There were also some Sahabah (RA) who were of the opinion that although wearing clothing of silk is Haraam, there was nothing wrong with sitting on silk rugs. It is also possible that the rugs were being used by the governors of the Byzantine Empire who were the former rulers of the region and the Sahabah (RA) were only temporarily using the quarters of these rulers until they could consolidate their own quarters.
